title: Finite schemes as limits of finite finitely presented closed models
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $p:T\to S$ a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then there exist a nonempty directed set $I$, schemes $T_i$ over $S$ with structure maps $p_i:T_i\to S$, compatible transition maps $r_{ji}:T_j\to T_i$ for $j\ge i$, and compatible $S$-morphisms $\pi_i:T\to T_i$, such that each $p_i$ is finite and of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated), each $r_{ji}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $(T,(\pi_i))$ is the inverse limit of this system in the category of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. In particular $p_i\circ\pi_i=p$ for every $i$.
